text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency SLO breach on /v1/generate-stream — p95=1.8s (SLO=1.2s), p99=4.2s. Streaming stalls observed (clients reporting stalled event stream frames). Cluster: gpu-prod-3. Auto-routing triggered fallback rules: partial. Tagging suspected hardware noise on node gpu-prod-3-node-7. Paging on-call.

Jessica: oncall here, seeing a spike across multiple models on that cluster. Customer error rate also up ~0.8%. Starting triage — collecting tail traces and kernel logs.

Carson: I'm pulling the p99 traces now, looks like tail latency correlates with long kernel wait on KV cache refill, but there's also a batch of `NVML ECC` warnings in logs from node-7.

Priya: can you paste the ECC logs? also checking telemetry for thermal events.

Carson: pasted snippet from node system journal: 
```
May 10 12:31:02 gpu-prod-3-node-7 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=0, Ch 00000010, engine GPC
May 10 12:31:02 gpu-prod-3-node-7 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, CE: single-bit ECC error
May 10 12:31:02 gpu-prod-3-node-7 kernel: thermal_zone0: critical temp reached
```

Alex: those Xid/31 CE entries usually mean degraded ECC page ops — can cause GPU stalls under load. Also seeing repeated `NVML: GPU has been lost` events at ~12:31:XX.

Maya: any customer impact flags to set? CS reporting a handful of timed-out streaming requests. I'm prepping communications.

Jessica: set impact to "partial degraded" for customers in eu-west and us-east using model variants on that cluster. Maya, send a short note: "We’ve detected latency spikes affecting streaming; mitigating now, ETA 30–60m."

Maya: on it.

Priya: I'm SSH'ing into node-7 to confirm thermal telemetry and GPU hw state: `ssh ops@gpu-prod-3-node-7` 

Priya: thermal sensors show GPU temp hitting 93C before fans spiked; fans respond but temperature climbs back. We may be hitting thermal throttling loop on that board. Also ECC counters increasing.

Alex: good catch. Plan: 1) drain node-7, 2) evac workloads to healthy nodes in the same AZ, 3) bring up fallback model variant with lower memory footprint for bursty streaming, 4) open hardware ticket for replacement.

Jessica: agree. We should also reduce batch sizes for the cluster briefly to cut peak power/temperature. Can runtime apply a temporary batching policy?

Alex: I can push a runtime config patch to reduce max batch size from 12 -> 6 for gpu-prod-3; will do a controlled rollout. Deploy-bot will show progress.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Alex — runtime-config: reduce-batch-gpu-prod-3 v2. Expected rollout 2m.

Alex: also switching streaming fallback for `/v1/generate-stream` to use `gpt-lite-1` for new sessions originating from routes hitting gpu-prod-3. That reduces memory and removes some long-kv-cache ops.

Carson: while that's happening, I'm preparing node drain commands so we can cordon node-7 safely: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-prod-3-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-prod-3-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Priya: hold briefly — kube shows a pod stuck terminating on node-7 tied to a long-lived gRPC stream. We'll preemptively send a graceful shutdown signal to runtime agent so it can flush KV caches for affected sessions.

Alex: sending graceful shutdown via runtime admin API: 
```
POST https://runtime-admin.prod.cluster/gpu-prod-3/node/gpu-prod-3-node-7/drain
{ "graceful": true, "timeout_seconds": 20 }
```

Carson: after signal, pods started terminating. Drain finished at 12:35:14. Node cordoned. Moving traffic.

Priya: hardware telemetry snapshot saved and uploaded to infra-ticket: https://tickets.internal/infra/INC-4821. ECC count increased by +12 in last 5m. Recommend RMA replacement — flaky GPU likely.

Jessica: setting incident severity to Sev2 (partial outage, user-visible latencies). On-call rotation handoff in 30m — @Alex you'll take follow-up?

Alex: I can take post-mitigation monitoring and lead hardware follow-up. Taking on-call.

Maya: CS note sent: "We’re mitigating a platform latency issue affecting streaming; we’ve drained one GPU node and routed new streaming sessions to healthy nodes and a fallback model. Expected recovery within 30–60 minutes. We'll update with timeline once hardware RMA is scheduled."

Carson: p99 tail decreased after drain and batch size change — new p95=0.9s, p99=1.6s for affected routes. Still seeing occasional reconnect spikes (clients see 502 when long streams were cut).

Jessica: that's expected for the pods that were terminated mid-stream — we need to mark those requests as "retriable" in logs for CS to replay if needed.

Priya: opening a replacement request with datacenter ops. Logged: node-7 GPU#0 flagged for return — serial 0xA7B2C. Ops ETA 2 business days for swap.

Alex: adding durable mitigation: pin model-serving on that cluster to `quantized-compat` kernels for the remaining nodes to reduce memory pressure; also enabling smaller KV cache TTL (from 60s -> 20s) to avoid heavy refill bursts. Rollout started.

deploy-bot: runtime-config rollout completed for reduce-batch and kv-ttl on gpu-prod-3.

Carson: running synthetic streaming tests now — throughput recovering and tail latencies stable. Will run 30m watch.

Maya: any customer followup item assignments?

Jessica: assign to Maya for external comms, Alex for postmortem and action items with infra, Priya to track hardware RMA, Carson to validate telemetry and remediation tests.

Maya: ack, will prepare a short post for customers tomorrow summarizing impact and mitigations.

Alex: immediate action items I'm tracking: 
- write post-incident note with timeline and telemetry (w/ ECC/thermal traces)
- add autoscaling rule to proactively evacuate nodes on sustained ECC errors
- validate quantization/kv-ttl changes don't cause quality regression (run eval subset)

Priya: infra items: 
- RMA GPU on node-7 and run burn-in tests on replacement
- review datacenter cooling logs for that rack (possible hot-spot)
- add NVML ECC counter alert threshold to catch earlier

Carson: SRE items: 
- automate marking terminated streaming requests as retriable in logs
- add a runtime health-check that detects repeated Xid/CE and triggers automatic drain policy

Jessica: good. We'll keep monitoring for 1 hour, if stable we drop to Sev3. Alex will keep ownership.

Alex: I'm leaving a monitoring watch: p95/p99 dashboards linked here: https://dashboards.internal/streams/gpu-prod-3. Current p95=0.89s p99=1.55s. Marking active mitigations in the incident ticket.

Maya: thanks team — CS loop closed for now, will reopen if customers escalate.

Carson: follow-up note: collected `dmesg` from node-7 pre-drain: 
```
[12:30:57] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, CE: single-bit ECC error
[12:31:00] NVRM: GPU panic: halting
[12:31:04] nvlink: thermal trip detected
```

Priya: saved hardware logs in ticket. Scheduling datacenter onsite check.

incident-bot: incident update recorded in #incidents channel; incident ID INC-4821. Severity: Sev2 -> watch.

Jessica: nice work. Temporary mitigations look effective. We'll reconvene for a short RCA doc tomorrow. Closing the active paging loop — if anything regresses, ping @Alex.

Alex: thanks — keeping watch.

Carson: 30m watch started at 12:36. Will post final status at 13:06.

Maya: final note to CS thread queued.

(End of thread)
